population_segments.name: Pregnant individuals with diabetes
population_segments.source_text:
Diabetes Care Volume 49, Supplement 1, January 2026 S321

# 15. Management of Diabetes in Pregnancy: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026

population_segments.name: Individuals with a history of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM)
synonyms: people with a history of GDM
population_segments.source_text: In individuals with a history of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) should seek preconception screening for diabetes and preconception care to identify and treat hyperglycemia and prevent congenital malformations and other adverse maternal and fetal outcomes.

population_segments.name: Individuals with preexisting diabetes planning a pregnancy
synonyms: people with preexisting diabetes planning a pregnancy
population_segments.source_text: Individuals with preexisting diabetes who are planning a pregnancy should ideally begin receiving interprofessional care prior to conception

population_segments.name: Individuals with preexisting diabetes who have become pregnant
synonyms: people with preexisting diabetes who have become pregnant
population_segments.source_text: Individuals with preexisting diabetes who are planning a pregnancy or who have become pregnant should be counseled on the risk of development of diabetic embryopathy

population_segments.name: Pregnant individuals with type 1 diabetes
population_segments.source_text: 15.11 Recommend CGM to pregnant individuals with type 1 diabetes. A In conjunction with aims to achieve traditional pre- and postprandial glycemic goals, CGM can reduce the risk for large-for-gestational-age infants and neonatal hypoglycemia in pregnancy complicated by type 1 diabetes. A

population_segments.name: Pregnant individuals with type 2 diabetes
population_segments.source_text: 15.17 Insulin should be used to manage type 1 diabetes in pregnancy A and is the preferred agent for the management of GDM A and type 2 diabetes in pregnancy. B

population_segments.name: Individuals with diabetes and childbearing potential
synonyms: people with diabetes and childbearing potential
population_segments.source_text: Starting at puberty and continuing in all people with diabetes and childbearing potential, preconception counseling should be incorporated into routine diabetes care. A

population_segments.name: Pregnant individuals with GDM
population_segments.source_text: 15.15 Lifestyle behavior change is an essential component of management of GDM and may suffice as treatment for many individuals. Insulin should be added if needed to achieve glycemic goals. A

population_segments.name: Pregnant individuals with diabetes and chronic hypertension
synonyms: pregnant people with diabetes and chronic hypertension
population_segments.source_text: 15.24 In pregnant individuals with diabetes and chronic hypertension, a blood pressure threshold <140/90 mmHg is recommended for initiation and titration of therapy for better pregnancy outcomes. A Therapy should be deintensified if blood pressure is <90/60 mmHg. E

specific_goals.name: Preconception A1C goal
specific_goals.source_text: Preconception counseling should address the importance of achieving glucose levels as close to normal as is safely possible without excessive hypoglycemia, ideally A1C <6.5% (<48 mmol/mol), to reduce the risk of congenital anomalies, preeclampsia, macrosomia, preterm birth, and other complications. A
specific_goals.rationale: to reduce the risk of congenital anomalies, preeclampsia, macrosomia, preterm birth, and other complications

specific_goals.name: Preconception glucose goals
specific_goals.source_text: The following preconception glucose goals have been advised: preprandial glucose 80–110 mg/dL (4.4–6.1 mmol/L) and 2 h postprandial glucose <155 mg/dL (<8.6 mmol/L) (31).
specific_goals.target_value: preprandial glucose 80–110 mg/dL (4.4–6.1 mmol/L) and 2 h postprandial glucose <155 mg/dL (<8.6 mmol/L)
specific_goals.rationale: Setting preconception glucose goals is helpful in guiding insulin dose adjustments.

specific_goals.name: Pregnancy glucose goals
specific_goals.source_text: 15.8 Fasting, preprandial, and postprandial blood glucose monitoring are recommended in individuals with diabetes in pregnancy to achieve optimal glucose levels. Glucose goals are fasting plasma glucose <95 mg/dL (<5.3 mmol/L) and either 1-h postprandial glucose <140 mg/dL (<7.8 mmol/mol) or 2-h postprandial glucose <120 mg/dL (<6.7 mmol/L). B
specific_goals.target_value: fasting plasma glucose <95 mg/dL (<5.3 mmol/L) and either 1-h postprandial glucose <140 mg/dL (<7.8 mmol/mol) or 2-h postprandial glucose <120 mg/dL (<6.7 mmol/L)

specific_goals.name: Pregnancy A1C goal
specific_goals.source_text: 15.9 Due to increased red blood cell turnover, A1C is slightly lower during pregnancy in people with and without diabetes. Ideally, the A1C goal in pregnancy is <6% (<42 mmol/mol) if this can be achieved without significant hypoglycemia, but the goal may be relaxed to <7% (<53 mmol/mol) if necessary to prevent hypoglycemia. B
specific_goals.target_value: <6% (<42 mmol/mol) or <7% (<53 mmol/mol) if necessary to prevent hypoglycemia
specific_goals.rationale: if this can be achieved without significant hypoglycemia

specific_goals.name: Pregnancy sensor glucose range
specific_goals.source_text:
Goals for sensor glucose ranges in pregnancy are:

• Goal sensor glucose range 63–140 mg/dL may not be sufficient to achieve glycemic goals. B

• (3.5–7.8 mmol/L): TIR, goal >70% Time below range (TBR) (<63 mg/dL [<3.5 mmol/L]): level 1 TBR, goal <4% TBR (<54 mg/dL [<3.0 mmol/L]): level 2 TBR, goal <1% TAR (>140 mg/dL [>7.8 mmol/L]): TAR, goal <25%
specific_goals.target_value: range 63–140 mg/dL (3.5–7.8 mmol/L): TIR, goal >70%; TBR (<63 mg/dL [<3.5 mmol/L]): level 1 TBR, goal <4%; TBR (<54 mg/dL [<3.0 mmol/L]): level 2 TBR, goal <1%; TAR (>140 mg/dL [>7.8 mmol/L]): TAR, goal <25%

specific_goals.name: Blood pressure goal in pregnant individuals with diabetes and chronic hypertension
synonyms: BP goal in pregnant individuals with diabetes and chronic hypertension
specific_goals.source_text: 15.24 In pregnant individuals with diabetes and chronic hypertension, a blood pressure threshold <140/90 mmHg is recommended for initiation and titration of therapy for better pregnancy outcomes. A Therapy should be deintensified if blood pressure is <90/60 mmHg. E

specific_goals.name: Blood pressure deintensification threshold in pregnant individuals with diabetes and chronic hypertension
synonyms: BP deintensification threshold in pregnant individuals with diabetes and chronic hypertension
specific_goals.source_text: 15.24 In pregnant individuals with diabetes and chronic hypertension, a blood pressure threshold <140/90 mmHg is recommended for initiation and titration of therapy for better pregnancy outcomes. A Therapy should be deintensified if blood pressure is <90/60 mmHg. E

allowed_medications.name: Insulin
allowed_medications.source_text: 15.17 Insulin should be used to manage type 1 diabetes in pregnancy A and is the preferred agent for the management of GDM A and type 2 diabetes in pregnancy. B
allowed_medications.special_instructions: Preferred agent for management of GDM and type 2 diabetes in pregnancy.

allowed_medications.name: Metformin in pregnancy
allowed_medications.source_text: When prepregnancy metformin use is continued in early pregnancy, it can be discontinued at the end of the first trimester (after organogenesis) to avoid sudden deterioration of glycemia and an associated increased risk of malformations due to hyperglycemia. Continuation of metformin in early pregnancy is considered safe, as first-trimester metformin use has not been associated with increased risk of major congenital malformations, and there is minimal maternal-to-fetal transfer of metformin in early gestation.
allowed_medications.special_instructions: Can be discontinued at the end of the first trimester. Considered safe in first-trimester use.

allowed_medications.name: Low-dose aspirin for preeclampsia prevention
allowed_medications.source_text: 15.23 Pregnant individuals with type 1 or type 2 diabetes should be prescribed low-dose aspirin 100–150 mg/day starting at 12–16 weeks of gestation to lower the risk of preeclampsia. A dosage of 162 mg/day may be acceptable; currently, in the U.S., low-dose aspirin is available in 81-mg tablets.
allowed_medications.special_instructions: 100–150 mg/day starting at 12–16 weeks of gestation to lower the risk of preeclampsia.

contraindicated_medications.name: ACE inhibitors in pregnancy
contraindicated_medications.source_text: 15.25a Potentially harmful medications in pregnancy (e.g., ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists) should be stopped prior to conception and avoided in sexually active individuals of childbearing potential who are not using reliable contraception. B

contraindicated_medications.name: Angiotensin receptor blockers in pregnancy
contraindicated_medications.source_text: 15.25a Potentially harmful medications in pregnancy (e.g., ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists) should be stopped prior to conception and avoided in sexually active individuals of childbearing potential who are not using reliable contraception. B

contraindicated_medications.name: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists in pregnancy
contraindicated_medications.source_text: 15.25a Potentially harmful medications in pregnancy (e.g., ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists) should be stopped prior to conception and avoided in sexually active individuals of childbearing potential who are not using reliable contraception. B

contraindicated_medications.name: Lipid-lowering medications in pregnancy
contraindicated_medications.source_text: 15.25b In most circumstances, lipid-lowering medications should be stopped prior to conception and avoided in sexually active individuals of childbearing potential with diabetes who are not using reliable contraception. B
contraindicated_medications.reason: Should be stopped prior to conception and avoided in sexually active individuals of childbearing potential with diabetes who are not using reliable contraception.

contraindicated_medications.name: GLP-1 RAs in pregnancy
contraindicated_medications.source_text: Glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and GLP-1 RAs should be discontinued prior to pregnancy, and contraception should be used while taking them (see section 9, “Pharmacologic Approaches to Glycemic Treatment”).
contraindicated_medications.reason: Should be discontinued prior to pregnancy, and contraception should be used while taking them.

contraindicated_medications.name: Dual GIP and GLP-1 RAs in pregnancy
contraindicated_medications.source_text: Glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and GLP-1 RAs should be discontinued prior to pregnancy, and contraception should be used while taking them (see section 9, “Pharmacologic Approaches to Glycemic Treatment”).
contraindicated_medications.reason: Should be discontinued prior to pregnancy, and contraception should be used while taking them.

contraindicated_medications.name: Metformin in pregnant individuals with hypertension or preeclampsia
contraindicated_medications.source_text: However, due to the potential for growth restriction or acidosis in the setting of placental insufficiency, metformin should not be used in pregnant people with hypertension or preeclampsia or those at risk for intrauterine growth restriction.
contraindicated_medications.reason: Due to the potential for growth restriction or acidosis in the setting of placental insufficiency.

contraindicated_medications.name: Glyburide in pregnancy
contraindicated_medications.source_text: Metformin and glyburide, individually or in combination, should not be used as first-line agents for management of diabetes in pregnancy, as both cross the placenta to the fetus A and.
contraindicated_medications.reason: Crosses the placenta to the fetus.
